name: Realization of the revised kilogram with NIST-4
description: The U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology used its NIST-4 Kibble balance to determine the masses of two travelling platinum-iridium standards from the fixed numerical value of the Planck constant.

places.note: National Institute of Standards and Technology

date.label: September–October 2019
date.basis: The NIST section of the final report dates the laboratory’s two series of measurements for each mass to these months.

events.statement: NIST used its fourth-generation Kibble balance in vacuum to determine the masses of travelling standards 85 and 104 for comparison CCM.M-K8.2019.
events.scope: Direct mass determinations after the new definition took effect. The BIPM made its own comparator measurements for the comparison.

contributions.group: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
contributions.resource: NIST-4 mass determinations on the two travelling standards.

evidence.supports: The report identifies masses 85 and 104 and records their direct NIST-4 weighings in vacuum in September and October 2019.
The report identifies masses 85 and 104 and records their direct NIST-4 weighings in vacuum in September and October 2019.
The protocol uses the SI’s exact h, and Table 4 reports measured masses and standard uncertainties.

date.label: 17 January–3 February 2025
date.basis: The section reports 17–27 January for K85 and 28 January–3 February for K104.

events.statement: NIST again determined the masses of K85 and K104 in vacuum with NIST-4. These measurements contributed to comparison CCM.M-K8.2024.

evidence.locator: Table 2 p. 6, §4.6 p. 9 and Table 5 p. 18
evidence.supports: NIST identified and measured K85 and K104 directly in vacuum with NIST-4 in January and February 2025. Table 5 reports the resulting values.

earliest_record.rationale: The earliest dated post-redefinition series for this implementation examined in the cited original operator and comparison records.

links.statement: The CCM.M-K8.2019 protocol used the revised SI’s fixed value of h to assign mass values from the NIST-4 realization measurements.
links.scope: The numerical input for the 2019 determinations of mass values on NIST-4. Construction of the balance and its earlier measurements of h are separate.

evidence.locator: Resolution 1, English pp. 472–474, decision and Appendices 1–3
evidence.supports: The revised definition took effect from 20 May 2019, replacing the IPK definition and fixing h exactly.
The comparison protocol specifies the exact fixed value and the report identifies the NIST-4 realization and which mass values it produced.

measures.subject: Travelling standard 85
measures.conditions: Measured under vacuum using the fixed Planck constant. Standard uncertainty 0.027 mg.

evidence.locator: Table 4, p. 13, row NIST 85, NMI realization columns
evidence.supports: Reports a mass offset of -0.7679 mg and standard uncertainty 0.027 mg.

measures.subject: Travelling standard 104
measures.conditions: Measured under vacuum using the fixed Planck constant. Standard uncertainty 0.0273 mg.

evidence.locator: Table 4, p. 13, row NIST 104, NMI realization columns
evidence.supports: Reports a mass offset of 0.398 mg and standard uncertainty 0.0273 mg.
